newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germann Lufthansa hit by new pay protests.
newsitem.headline: Germann Lufthansa hit by new pay protests.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG was hit by worker protests at a number airports across Germany in its long-running pay dispute with employees, the airline said on Thursday.
White-collar worker union DAG said it had called on all of its ground personnel and flight crews to walk off the job for two hours, between 0530 and 0730 GMT this morning.
A union spokesman said some 100 flights would be affected by the action, targeted at eight German airports.

Lufthansa has some 50,000 employees but the union declined to give an estimate of how many people would be stopping work. Lufthansa said 16 intra-German flights have been cancelled but that the airline would be using large-bodied jets, like the Airbus A340, to attempt to avoid massive delays.

"On the most important routes we are using extra large planes to take account of the situation and we hope to have things back to normal very soon. Delays however cannot be ruled out," Lufthansa spokesman Christian Klick said.
The union said that Germany's eight largest airports, including Frankfurt, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg and Duesseldorf, would be affected by the work stoppage.

Lufthansa however said some Frankfurt staff have ignored the calls to walk off the job. "To the best of my knowledge Lufthansa personnel in Frankfurt has not followed the calls to walk off the job, and flight preparations are proceeding close to schedule. However there are delays in the flights acutally getting off the ground," Klick said.
DAG, in a long-running pay dispute with Lufthansa, last month held brief stoppages that cost the airline some 12 million marks as 35 flights had to be cancelled.
Sources close to airline staff had said on Tuesday that the protests are likely to hit international traffic as well as the domestic traffic involved in the first protest.
They added that if Lufthansa refused to change its position as a result, a ballot on all-out strike action could follow.

DAG, which shares representation of the airline's 50,000 staff with the transport and public sector union OeTV, has said Lufthansa has still not offered its members a 1997 wage increase in line with others in the industry.

It is also angry that Lufthansa wants the new contracts to last 27 months instead of a year. Given the threat that many Lufthansa jobs could be moved abroad, the union would not tie itself to a two-year contract, DAG has said.
Lufthansa on Wednesday described the scheduled protest as "completely incomprehensible" and said that such a move would not force it to alter its position.
